name: Cadmium Green
lede: Cadmium green is the name of a composite artist's green, a blend of a cadmium yellow with viridian rather than a single mineral.

sections.title: A mixture, not a mineral
sections.body:
Paterson describes cadmium green as made by mixing cadmium yellow and viridian [1]. The Pigment Compendium agrees in spirit: it cites a 1928 source for the term as a composite pigment based on a cadmium yellow [2]. The yellow half is a sulphide first made in 1820 and used extensively by artists [1]. So the name tells you the recipe, not a deposit or a plant.

Compare [[cadmium-lemon]] and [[cadmium-orange]], the same cadmium family, and [[viridian]], its green partner [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is rare in museum canvases. It appears in 0.08% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (19 paintings, as photographed) [3]. The earliest in our data is 1875 and the latest 1918, but the early centuries are thin, so that is a floor, not a first [3].

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "cadmium green"

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "cadmium green", "cadmium yellow"

questions.q: According to Paterson, cadmium green is made by mixing cadmium yellow with what?
True or false: the earliest cadmium-green painting in our archive is a firm first for the color.

openers: The name is a recipe: cadmium yellow mixed with viridian.

issues: Lede said blue-green; sources say viridian
